subject.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss

question: Should Discord retain an outer reply-session initialization-conflict retry after the shared recovery proposal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 is resolved?
rationale: Both recovery layers are plausible, but permanent layering changes aggregate attempts, latency, session-state writes, and transport cleanup; repository evidence cannot determine whether that defense-in-depth is intentional.

options.title: Shared recovery first
options.body: Resolve the common-owner self-heal, then retain Discord retry only if live proof demonstrates a remaining channel-specific failure window.

options.title: Narrow layered recovery
options.body: Keep both only after separating non-idempotent setup from retryable dispatch and defining the aggregate retry budget.

options.title: Discord-only recovery
options.body: Use this channel-level retry and decline shared recovery for the same conflict class.

recommendation.title: Shared recovery first
recommendation.body: Resolve the common-owner self-heal, then retain Discord retry only if live proof demonstrates a remaining channel-specific failure window.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans Discord processing, shared session lifecycle, and the closest merged channel-level retry precedent.
